The work involves evaluating the reliability, accuracy and the feasibility of alternative methodologies for designing and setting up complex and integrated surveys and supporting infrastructures. Effort: Intellectual Effort

The work involves evaluating the reliability, accuracy and the feasibility of alternative methodologies for designing and setting up complex and integrated surveys and supporting infrastructures. Many survey systems are unique and contain unique components and solutions to problems push the limits of available technology and statistical methodology. Solutions to typical survey design problems go well beyond the straightforward application of standard design practices and can require considerable ingenuity and creativity to solve. Survey development and implementation can be constrained by client requirements or conflicting priorities of other stakeholders who must be convinced of the benefits to be derived from the suggested approaches, procedures and methods, and also by respondents' concerns for privacy of sensitive information and respondent burden. Further constraints involve the requirement to respect deadlines, resources, changing priorities and operational barriers when working on more than one project at a time.
Investigates new statistical methodology and techniques and computer methods to evaluate their usefulness and assess their feasibility and the impact of their application for Statistics Canada.
Transforms client needs and requirements into methodology requirements necessary to accomplish project objectives.
Assesses the methodological requirements of a project and matches its development to staff to maximize the use of their existing skill sets.

Assesses alternatives and evaluates the benefits of changing methodology with respect to statistical reliability, accuracy and feasibility and determines how methodological (statistical, survey, geographical, quality assurance, time series, analytical) aspects of surveys or supporting infrastructure should be developed or re-designed. The outcome can be constrained by clients or other service areas that must be convinced of the benefits and to change their procedures and methods. This work is performed under client pressure to respect deadlines, budgets and operational constraints, while working on more than one project at a time.

Determines the significance of the improvements obtained when applying new methods to surveys or supporting infrastructures in the particular social or economic program area, while researching improvement to the cost, timeliness and quality.

Determines the framework to be used in the development of methodology required to accomplish project objectives. It is influenced by deliverables and the manner in which they should relate to each other, by the assignment of skill sets and the number of persons working towards expected outcomes of the project, by the choice of methods and procedures that may sometimes be less familiar to project members, and by time and cost options available.

Defines and sets priorities and milestones, allocates, resolves conflicting priorities and manages the human and financial resources of a section or project. This effort is increased by the fact that a number of projects are managed concurrently and projects are often conducted under tight deadlines with a number of conflicting priorities, and involve multi-disciplinary project teams where a consensus must be reached between team members. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other projects.

Decides on remedial courses of action (from fine-tuning to significant change) to solve technical difficulties arising during implementation. Technical difficulties arise when abnormal circumstances occur that could not be foreseen in original planning assumptions (e.g. changes to coverage areas, unavailability of respondents due to extreme weather, extreme growth or shrinkage in the frame).
Balances the need to develop new methods to solve particular problems with the use of more generalized methods or approaches.
Proposes pilot tests to assess performance of components under study and determines the appropriate information required that would support the continued development of the component.

Identifies and defines opportunities or specific problem areas related to the assigned statistical information program where new or refined statistical and methodological methods could be applied. Reviews the state of existing knowledge. Synthesizes and assesses defensible and feasible new methods for application.

Adapts methods and procedures of existing survey and support systems or initiates and develops new methods and procedures to meet newly identified statistical information program needs, within time and cost constraints.

Key Activities: Manages a methodology research section engaged in activities in survey methodology, mathematical statistics, computational statistics, data analysis methods or mathematical procedures.
Provides expert methodological advice and consultation on the design, development and application of methods for statistical information programs.
Plans, develops and manages detailed evaluation studies to improve statistical survey methodology at Statistics Canada.

Initiates, conducts and publishes research, often jointly with academics, to develop new methods of sampling, collection, estimation, editing, imputation, survey data analysis and other survey related methodologies.
Augments corporate professional expertise through the exchange of technical information and survey experience with professionals in other statistical agencies, universities and foreign countries.
Determines topics and promotes research in survey methods, often jointly with academics.

Responsibility: Information for the Use of Others

Researches and recommends the methodological and statistical frameworks for data gathering processes for census, survey or administrative data sources to meet the statistical information program needs of clients.
Explains the methodologies, their potential, limitations and applicability in the development and integration of surveys or phases of surveys for clients as input to their analytical requirements.
Research on new methods and techniques of data collection, processing and analysis to identify potential benefits in terms of cost, timeliness and quality for existing or new surveys.
Provides expert advice on new statistical methods to clients involved in providing statistical information as specified in legislation for service to the people of Canada.
Proposes revisions to statistical methods and techniques based on research to clients to enhance or improve existing statistical information products.

Prepares comprehensive research reports detailing proposed procedures and methodologies for steering committees, external advisory committees and other departments to be used to assess survey programs and to make recommendations concerning redesign or new development to those surveys that will impact departmental programs.

Adds to the pool of knowledge within the department through exchanging technical information, survey experiences and results of research with professionals in other departments, statistical agencies and universities of Canada and foreign countries.

Researches, prepares and writes technical reports and papers for publication or presentation at conferences or seminars, and course material in survey methodology for departmental and outside clients to promote the use of good statistical methods.
Recommending topics and invitees for symposia and workshops on statistics and survey methodology for use by the organizing committee.

As an expert consultant on new methods, provides instruction and guidance to researchers in the field about new statistical technology, state of the art research and new experimental methods to improve the level of science.
Provides peer reviews of research papers and review articles for scientific journals to assist the journal editors in deciding which are suitable for publication.
Creates or adds to the body of scientific statistical knowledge for use by practitioners in improving the efficiency, effectiveness and reliability of statistical information systems.
Proposes and recommends the skill levels and resources required to carry out the section’s research responsibilities.
Money
Budgeting:

Plans and develops a budget for the section in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. This responsibility includes determining the allocation of methodological and operational input to research projects in progress and also for proposed projects submitted as part of the Long Term Planning Process.
Tracks time spent on projects vis-a-vis progress on deliverables compared to consumption.
Money flow:
Manages time spent for cost recovery activities for the purpose of recovering such costs from the client.
Spending Funds:
Negotiates and arranges contracts with consulting firms, universities and professional statisticians for the acquisition of professional statistical services or research fellowships.

Recommends expenditures for the acquisition of statistical books, reference materials or software and printing to carry out methodology projects; training and attendance by staff at conferences for professional development.
While in travel status, spends funds according to limits set out in the Travel Directives.
Physical Assets and Products

Ensures the protection of confidential information, contained in working files and paper copies, acquired in the research process and takes responsibility for their proper disposal or destruction after use. These active items are used, by own and other staff, in the production of information products for use by internal and external clients.

Organizes, on a rotating basis, international symposia and workshops related to new statistical and survey methodology for the exchange of information on current experience and research developments amongst invitees and others interested in statistics and survey methodology.
Ensuring Compliance

Evaluates and ensures application of procedures and practices developed by staff for use by survey statisticians, technicians and processing staff to abide by disclosure provisions or prevent breach of confidentiality, of data cells or data sets, as stipulated in the Statistics Act. Advises staff on acceptability of proposed actions. The unintentional release of confidential information can cause significant loss of good will as well as jeopardizing respondent relations.

Points out to clients the requirements of Statistics Canada’s policies relevant to statistical methodology such as The Review Of Information Products, Record Linkage or standards and guidelines for non-response.
Skills: Job Content Knowledge

The work requires knowledge of and research skill in the theory, principles and application of mathematics, statistics and survey methodology including recent developments, described in current literature and through contacts with other methodologists inside and outside the department, as they apply to:

Survey sampling methods including: use and maintenance of sampling frames, stratification, sample size determination and allocation, sample selection, multistage sampling, multiphase sampling, area sampling, sample rotation, weighting and estimation, variance estimation, use of modelling, and techniques to measure and assess sampling and non-sampling errors in surveys. This knowledge is required to meet the section’s responsibility to provide methodology research advice and service (including advancing the science and developing new methods for the Canadian statistical system) to departmental managers of statistical programs and to sponsoring clients, with specific information needs, in other government departments and the private sector.

Data collection principles and methods to initiate and promote the design of sampling schemes, design of pilot surveys, cognitive testing of questionnaires and manuals and design of components of data collection systems.

Probability theory and mathematical statistics to lead a section to design sampling frames and sample schemes, to develop methods for imputation, to develop and apply methods of record linkage, and to develop new methods of survey methodology.
Edit and imputation methods and automated coding systems for application in surveys and components of survey support infrastructure methods and automated coding methods for surveys.
Techniques for maintaining good respondent relations and for minimising respondent burden in the design of sampling schemes, interview procedures and in developing new methods of survey methodology.
Methods for the analysis of data from surveys with complex designs (e.g. involving stratification, multistage sampling, multiphase sampling, etc.)

Quality assurance and quality control methods, record linkage methods, time series methods, and disclosure avoidance techniques to ensure that methodology is developed that will assure the accuracy and confidentiality needs of the survey sponsor and to facilitate analysis.

Operations research, multivariate statistical methods, design of experiments, analysis methods for categorical and continuous data to advance the design and conduct of analytical and evaluation studies (of data from complex surveys, both cross-sectional and longitudinal) and of pilot surveys.

Recent developments in statistics and survey methodology, as described in current literature and through contacts with other methodologists inside and outside the department, to conduct developmental work to benefit surveys.
